stem: Bilal has a mixture of chalk powder, common salt, and water. He needs pure chalk powder and pure salt as separate products.

parts.text: Which plan correctly separates the mixture?

options.text: Filter to remove the chalk powder, then evaporate the filtrate to recover the salt.
Use one careful filtration alone to obtain pure chalk powder, pure salt, and pure water all at once.
Evaporate all the water first, then filter the dry chalk-and-salt powder to collect pure salt.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Chalk powder is insoluble so filtration removes it; salt stays dissolved and is recovered by evaporating the filtrate. One method alone cannot give both pure products.

teacher.key_rationale: A mixture with chalk powder, salt, and water needs a sequence: filter the insoluble chalk, then evaporate to get salt. Filtration alone leaves salt in water; evaporating first leaves a dry chalk–salt mix that filtration cannot purify.
